source.text: כִּ֗י הִנֵּ֛ה בַּיָּמִ֥ים הָהֵ֖מָּה וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת־שְׁב֥וּת יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For look, in those days and at that time, when I restore [the] fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

en.L: For look, in those days and at that time, \q when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,
en.B: For in those days and at that time, \q when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,
en.R: In those days, at that time, \q I will make things good again for Judah and Jerusalem.

es.L: Porque he aquí, en aquellos días y en aquel tiempo, \q cuando yo restaure la suerte de Judá y de Jerusalén,
es.B: Porque en aquellos días y en aquel tiempo, \q cuando yo restaure la suerte de Judá y de Jerusalén,
es.R: En aquellos días, en ese tiempo, \q haré que todo vuelva a ir bien para Judá y Jerusalén.

decisions.choice: This verse is 4:1 in the Hebrew text, 3:1 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins its fourth chapter here. Many Bibles number this chapter 3, so their 3:1-21 is 4:1-21 here, and their 2:28-32 is 3:1-5 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Joel is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes: turn things around, bring back what was lost
decisions.reason: The phrase means to reverse a people's ruin and make their life good again (Deuteronomy 30:3; Jeremiah 29:14; Hosea 6:11). It was once rendered "bring back the captivity", because it often includes the return of exiles. The written text and the reading tradition differ by one letter in the verb, with no change of sense.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 2
decisions.reason: "When I restore" sets the time; the main clause, "I will gather all the nations", comes in verse 2.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes (L, B); make things good again (R); a comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the wording set in Jeremiah. Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma, since the sentence continues; Readable makes it a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: "restaurar la suerte" (L, B); "hacer que todo vuelva a ir bien" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Spanish terms note sets from Psalms 14:7 and 126:4, and as Ezekiel 29:14 and 39:25 have it.

decisions.choice: Hebrew 4:1-21 is English 3:1-21
decisions.reason: The Spanish follows the Hebrew numbering, as the English does; the meaning footnote gives the other numbering.

source.text: וְקִבַּצְתִּי֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְה֣וֹרַדְתִּ֔ים אֶל־עֵ֖מֶק יְהֽוֹשָׁפָ֑ט וְנִשְׁפַּטְתִּ֨י עִמָּ֜ם שָׁ֗ם עַל־עַמִּ֨י וְנַחֲלָתִ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּזְּר֣וּ בַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְאֶת־אַרְצִ֖י חִלֵּֽקוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will gather all the nations and bring them down to [the] valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will enter into judgment with them there on account of my people and my inheritance Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations; and my land they have divided.

en.L: I will gather all the nations \q and bring them down \q into the valley of Jehoshaphat, \q and I will enter into judgment with them there on account of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land they have divided up.
en.B: I will gather all the nations \q and bring them down \q into the valley of Jehoshaphat. \q There I will bring them to judgment on behalf of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, \q and because they divided up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land.
en.R: I will bring all the nations together \q and take them down \q to the valley of Jehoshaphat. \q There I will judge them for what they did to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They scattered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people among the nations, \q and they divided up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land among themselves.

es.L: reuniré a todas las naciones \q y las haré descender \q al valle de Josafat, \q y allí entraré en juicio con ellas a causa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo y de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} heredad, Israel, a quien dispersaron entre las naciones, \q y se repartieron {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra.
es.B: reuniré a todas las naciones \q y las haré bajar \q al valle de Josafat. \q Allí las llevaré a juicio en defensa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} heredad, Israel, a quien dispersaron entre las naciones, \q y porque se repartieron {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra.
es.R: Reuniré a todas las naciones \q y las llevaré \q al valle de Josafat. \q Allí las juzgaré por lo que le hicieron a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenece. Dispersaron a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo entre las naciones, \q y se repartieron {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra entre ellos.

decisions.choice: the valley of Jehoshaphat: the name means "the LORD judges"
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat means "the LORD has judged" or "the LORD judges". The verb that follows, "I will enter into judgment", comes from the same root, so the name says what will happen there. In verse 14 the same place is "the valley of decision".

decisions.choice: where the valley was: not known
alternatives: the Kidron Valley east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: No valley of this name is mentioned elsewhere in the Old Testament, and it may be a name for the place of judgment rather than a place on the map. From early Christian times the name was given to the Kidron Valley, between Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives. Some connect it with King Jehoshaphat, whose enemies destroyed one another when the LORD fought for him (2 Chronicles 20:20-26).

decisions.choice: scattered among the nations, the land divided: exile and the loss of the land
decisions.reason: The nations are charged with deporting the people of Israel and Judah and parceling out their land among themselves. This describes the Assyrian and Babylonian conquests and the exile that followed (2 Kings 17:6; 25:11), and the neighboring peoples who took over parts of the land (Ezekiel 35:10; 36:5).

decisions.choice: my inheritance Israel: the people the LORD has made his own
decisions.reason: As in 2:17, the LORD calls his people his inheritance. The charge is not only what the nations did to Israel but what they did to the LORD's own people and land.

decisions.choice: the valley of Jehoshaphat (all levels)
decisions.reason: As set for the Twelve, the name is kept at every level, with a footnote giving its meaning (m1).

decisions.choice: "el valle de Josafat"
decisions.reason: The name is kept at every level, as the terms note sets; the meaning footnote explains it as "the LORD judges".

source.text: וְאֶל־עַמִּ֖י יַדּ֣וּ גוֹרָ֑ל וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ הַיֶּ֨לֶד֙ בַּזּוֹנָ֔ה וְהַיַּלְדָּ֛ה מָכְר֥וּ בַיַּ֖יִן וַיִּשְׁתּֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And for my people they have cast a lot, and they have given the boy for a prostitute, and the girl they have sold for wine, and they have drunk.

en.L: And for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people they cast lots; \q they gave a boy for a prostitute, \q and sold a girl for wine, and drank [it].
en.B: They cast lots for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q They traded boys for prostitutes \q and sold girls for wine to drink.
en.R: They threw lots to divide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people among themselves as slaves. \q They traded boys for prostitutes. \q They sold girls to buy wine, and they drank it.

es.L: Y por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo echaron suertes; \q dieron un muchacho por una prostituta, \q y vendieron una muchacha por vino, y [lo] bebieron.
es.B: Echaron suertes sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. \q Cambiaron muchachos por prostitutas \q y vendieron muchachas por vino para beber.
es.R: Echaron suertes para repartirse a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo como esclavos. \q Cambiaron muchachos por prostitutas. \q Vendieron muchachas para comprar vino, y se lo bebieron.

decisions.choice: cast lots: divide prisoners of war as slaves
decisions.reason: After a battle the victors cast lots for the captives, to share them out as slaves (Obadiah 11; Nahum 3:10).

decisions.choice: a boy for a prostitute, a girl for wine: children sold for a night's pleasure
decisions.reason: The captured children were sold for the price of a prostitute or of a drink of wine. The verse shows the contempt in which the nations held the LORD's people.

decisions.choice: to divide my people among themselves as slaves (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says why the lots were cast (m1).

source.text: וְ֠גַם מָה־אַתֶּ֥ם לִי֙ צֹ֣ר וְצִיד֔וֹן וְכֹ֖ל גְּלִיל֣וֹת פְּלָ֑שֶׁת הַגְּמ֗וּל אַתֶּם֙ מְשַׁלְּמִ֣ים עָלָ֔י וְאִם־גֹּמְלִ֤ים אַתֶּם֙ עָלַ֔י קַ֣ל מְהֵרָ֔ה אָשִׁ֥יב גְּמֻלְכֶ֖ם בְּרֹאשְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And also what [are] you to me, Tyre and Sidon and all [the] regions of Philistia? [Is it] a recompense you [are] repaying to me? And if you [are] paying [it] to me, swiftly, speedily I will return your recompense on your head.

en.L: And also, what [are] you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Tyre and Sidon \q and all the districts of Philistia? \q Are you repaying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a recompense? \q And if you are paying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} back, \q swiftly, speedily \q I will return your recompense on your head.
en.B: What are you to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Tyre and Sidon \q and all you regions of Philistia? \q Are you paying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} back for something? \q If you are paying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} back, \q swiftly and speedily \q I will turn your deeds back on your own heads.
en.R: People of Tyre and Sidon and all the regions of Philistia, \q what do you have against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q Are you trying to pay {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} back for something? \q If you are, I will very quickly pay you back for what you have done.

es.L: Y además, ¿qué [son] {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, Tiro y Sidón \q y todas las regiones de Filistea? \q ¿Acaso {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:están|estáis}} pagando una retribución? \q Y si {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:están|estáis}} pagando, \q pronto, muy pronto \q haré recaer {{plural_you:su retribución sobre su cabeza|vuestra retribución sobre vuestra cabeza}}.
es.B: ¿Qué tienen que ver {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} conmigo, Tiro y Sidón \q y todas las regiones de Filistea? \q ¿Acaso {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:están|estáis}} devolviendo algo? \q Si {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} lo {{plural_you:están|estáis}} devolviendo, \q pronto y sin demora \q haré que {{plural_you:sus acciones caigan sobre su propia cabeza|vuestras acciones caigan sobre vuestra propia cabeza}}.
es.R: Gente de Tiro y Sidón y de todas las regiones de Filistea, \q ¿qué {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}? \q ¿{{plural_you:Quieren|Queréis}} vengarse de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} por algo? \q Si es así, muy pronto {{plural_you:les|os}} pagaré por lo que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} hecho.

decisions.choice: Tyre, Sidon and Philistia: the trading peoples of the coast
decisions.reason: Tyre and Sidon were the great Phoenician ports to the north, and the Philistine cities lay on the coast to the south-west of Judah. Both traded in slaves: Amos accuses Gaza and Tyre of handing over whole communities to Edom (Amos 1:6, 9), and Tyre traded in human beings with Javan, the Greeks (Ezekiel 27:13).

decisions.choice: what are you to me?: what quarrel do you have with me?
decisions.reason: The question asks what claim or grievance the other has (Judges 11:12; 2 Samuel 16:10). What these peoples did to Judah, they did to the LORD.

decisions.choice: recompense: repayment for what someone has done
decisions.reason: The word means what someone deserves for his deeds, good or bad. The LORD asks if they think they are paying him back for some wrong. He will pay them back instead: what they did will come back on their own heads (Obadiah 15; Psalm 7:17).

decisions.choice: turn your deeds back on your own heads (B); pay you back for what you have done (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "return your recompense on your head" means. The same wording is used in verse 7.

decisions.choice: plural_you to Tyre, Sidon and Philistia
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks to the coastal peoples in the plural, so every "you" in verses 4-8 has a plural_you span; "conmigo" (B) is God's own pronoun in a form with no free capital, so it takes no deity_pronoun span.

source.text: אֲשֶׁר־כַּסְפִּ֥י וּזְהָבִ֖י לְקַחְתֶּ֑ם וּמַֽחֲמַדַּי֙ הַטֹּבִ֔ים הֲבֵאתֶ֖ם לְהֵיכְלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who my silver and my gold have taken, and my desirable good things have brought into your temples.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} silver and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} gold you have taken, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} precious treasures \q you have carried into your temples.
en.B: You took {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} silver and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} gold, \q and carried off {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} finest treasures \q into your temples.
en.R: You took {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} silver and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} gold. \q You carried off {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} best treasures \q and put them in your temples.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:ustedes tomaron|vosotros tomasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} plata y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} oro, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} tesoros preciosos \q {{plural_you:llevaron|llevasteis}} a {{plural_you:sus templos|vuestros templos}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tomaron|Tomasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} plata y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} oro, \q y {{plural_you:se llevaron|os llevasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mejores tesoros \q a {{plural_you:sus templos|vuestros templos}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tomaron|Tomasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} plata y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} oro. \q {{plural_you:Se llevaron|Os llevasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mejores tesoros \q y los {{plural_you:pusieron|pusisteis}} en {{plural_you:sus templos|vuestros templos}}.

decisions.choice: my silver and my gold: the LORD's treasures, plundered by the nations
decisions.reason: Everything of value belongs to the LORD (Haggai 2:8), and the temple treasures were his in a special way. When Jerusalem was plundered, its treasures were carried away (1 Kings 14:26; 2 Kings 24:13; 25:13-17). Conquerors put captured treasures in the temples of their own gods (2 Chronicles 36:7; Ezra 1:7).

decisions.choice: your temples: or your palaces
decisions.reason: The word means a large building, either a temple or a palace. Next to the LORD's treasures, temples are most likely meant.

decisions.choice: and put them in (R)
decisions.reason: Readable completes the picture of carrying the treasures into the temples.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ וּבְנֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם מְכַרְתֶּ֖ם לִבְנֵ֣י הַיְּוָנִ֑ים לְמַ֥עַן הַרְחִיקָ֖ם מֵעַ֥ל גְּבוּלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem you have sold to the children of the Greeks, in order to remove them far from their border.

en.L: And the people of Judah and the people of Jerusalem \q you have sold to the Greeks, \q to remove them far from their own border.
en.B: You sold the people of Judah and of Jerusalem to the Greeks, \q to send them far away from their own land.
en.R: You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem as slaves to the Greeks. \q You sent them far away from their homeland.

es.L: Y a los hijos de Judá y a los hijos de Jerusalén \q {{plural_you:los vendieron|los vendisteis}} a los griegos, \q para alejarlos de su propia frontera.
es.B: {{plural_you:Vendieron|Vendisteis}} a la gente de Judá y de Jerusalén a los griegos, \q para mandarlos lejos de su propia tierra.
es.R: {{plural_you:Vendieron|Vendisteis}} como esclavos a los griegos a la gente de Judá y de Jerusalén. \q {{plural_you:Los enviaron|Los enviasteis}} lejos de su patria.

decisions.choice: the Greeks: the Ionian Greeks of the Aegean coasts and islands
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name is Javan (Genesis 10:2, 4), the Ionians, Greeks of the west coast of Asia Minor and the Aegean islands. Ezekiel 27:13 lists Javan among Tyre's partners in the slave trade. Greek traders were active in the eastern Mediterranean from the eighth century BC on.

decisions.choice: to remove them far from their border: so that they could never come home
decisions.reason: Selling them to a distant people meant they would never return. The LORD answers in verse 7 by rousing them to come back from wherever they were sold.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah (all levels); the Greeks (all levels)
decisions.reason: "Children of" means the people of a place. Literal and Balanced say "the Greeks" for "the children of the Greeks", and Readable adds "as slaves", which the selling implies.

decisions.choice: "los griegos"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the sons of the Yevanim"; Spanish says "los griegos" at every level, as the English "the Greeks", and keeps "Javán" for the name in the lists of nations.

source.text: הִנְנִ֣י מְעִירָ֔ם מִן־הַ֨מָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁר־מְכַרְתֶּ֥ם אֹתָ֖ם שָׁ֑מָּה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֥י גְמֻלְכֶ֖ם בְּרֹאשְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Here I am rousing them from the place where you sold them there, and I will return your recompense on your head.

en.L: Look, I am rousing them \q from the place \q where you sold them, \q and I will return your recompense on your head.
en.B: But now I am stirring them up \q to leave the place \q where you sold them, \q and I will turn your deeds back on your own heads.
en.R: But now I am going to call them \q to come back from the places \q where you sold them. \q I will pay you back for what you have done.

es.L: He aquí, yo los despierto \q del lugar \q donde {{plural_you:los vendieron|los vendisteis}}, \q y haré recaer {{plural_you:su retribución sobre su cabeza|vuestra retribución sobre vuestra cabeza}}.
es.B: Pero ahora yo los pongo en marcha \q para que salgan del lugar \q donde {{plural_you:los vendieron|los vendisteis}}, \q y haré que {{plural_you:sus acciones caigan sobre su propia cabeza|vuestras acciones caigan sobre vuestra propia cabeza}}.
es.R: Pero ahora voy a llamarlos \q para que regresen de los lugares \q donde {{plural_you:los vendieron|los vendisteis}}. \q Y {{plural_you:les|os}} pagaré por lo que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} hecho.

decisions.choice: I am rousing them: stirring the captives to return home
decisions.reason: The verb means to wake or stir up. The people sold into slavery will be roused to come back from where they were taken. The same verb is used in verses 9 and 12 for rousing the nations to war.

decisions.choice: I will return your recompense on your head: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: The line repeats the end of verse 4. Verse 8 says how: they will suffer what they did.

decisions.choice: the same wording as in verse 4
decisions.reason: Each level repeats the wording of the end of verse 4. Balanced and Readable supply "But now" for the contrast and say "to leave" or "come back", the sense of rousing them.

source.text: וּמָכַרְתִּ֞י אֶת־בְּנֵיכֶ֣ם וְאֶת־בְּנֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם בְּיַד֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וּמְכָר֥וּם לִשְׁבָאיִ֖ם אֶל־גּ֣וֹי רָח֑וֹק כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will sell your sons and your daughters into [the] hand of [the] children of Judah, and they will sell them to [the] Sabeans, to a nation far away; for Yahweh has spoken.

en.L: I will sell your sons and daughters into the hand of Judah's people, \q and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a nation far away; \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.
en.B: I will sell your sons and daughters to the people of Judah, \q who will sell them to the Sabeans, a distant nation. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.
en.R: I will let the people of Judah buy your sons and daughters as slaves, \q and they will sell them to the Sabeans, a nation far away. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said this.

es.L: Venderé {{plural_you:sus hijos y sus hijas|vuestros hijos y vuestras hijas}} en mano de los hijos de Judá, \q y ellos los venderán a los sabeos, a una nación lejana; \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hablado.
es.B: Venderé {{plural_you:sus hijos y sus hijas|vuestros hijos y vuestras hijas}} a la gente de Judá, \q que los venderá a los sabeos, una nación lejana. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ha dicho.
es.R: Dejaré que la gente de Judá compre como esclavos a {{plural_you:sus hijos y sus hijas|vuestros hijos y vuestras hijas}}, \q y ellos los venderán a los sabeos, una nación lejana. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ha dicho.

decisions.choice: the Sabeans: the people of Sheba in southern Arabia
decisions.reason: Sheba lay in south-western Arabia, in what is now Yemen. Its people were great traders (1 Kings 10:1-2; Jeremiah 6:20; Ezekiel 27:22). The Greeks lay far to the west, the Sabeans far to the south-east.

decisions.choice: the punishment fits the crime
decisions.reason: Those who sold the children of Judah will have their own children sold. The law's rule that the penalty should match the wrong (Exodus 21:23-25; Obadiah 15) is applied to whole nations.

decisions.choice: for the LORD has spoken: the word is settled
decisions.reason: The phrase closes an oracle and puts the LORD's authority behind it (Isaiah 1:20; 22:25; Obadiah 18).

decisions.choice: sell ... to the people of Judah (B); let the people of Judah buy ... as slaves (R)
decisions.reason: "Sell into the hand of" means to hand over by sale. Readable says plainly what happens.

decisions.choice: "los sabeos"
decisions.reason: As Isaiah 45:14 in Spanish.

source.text: קִרְאוּ־זֹאת֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם קַדְּשׁ֖וּ מִלְחָמָ֑ה הָעִ֨ירוּ֙ הַגִּבּוֹרִ֔ים יִגְּשׁ֣וּ יַֽעֲל֔וּ כֹּ֖ל אַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Proclaim this among the nations: Consecrate war! Rouse the warriors! Let draw near, let come up all the men of war.

en.L: Proclaim this among the nations: \q Consecrate war; \q rouse the warriors; \q let them draw near, let them come up, \q all the men of war.
en.B: Announce this among the nations: \q Prepare for holy war! \q Rouse the warriors! \q Let them come forward and march up, \q all the fighting men.
en.R: Announce this to the nations: \q Get ready for war! \q Call out your best soldiers! \q Let all your fighting men come forward and march!

es.L: {{plural_you:Proclamen|Proclamad}} esto entre las naciones: \q {{plural_you:Consagren|Consagrad}} la guerra; \q {{plural_you:despierten|despertad}} a los valientes; \q que se acerquen, que suban \q todos los hombres de guerra.
es.B: {{plural_you:Anuncien|Anunciad}} esto entre las naciones: \q ¡{{plural_you:Prepárense|Preparaos}} para la guerra santa! \q ¡{{plural_you:Despierten|Despertad}} a los guerreros! \q Que se acerquen y avancen \q todos los hombres de combate.
es.R: {{plural_you:Anuncien|Anunciad}} esto a las naciones: \q ¡{{plural_you:Prepárense|Preparaos}} para la guerra! \q ¡{{plural_you:Llamen|Llamad}} a {{plural_you:sus mejores soldados|vuestros mejores soldados}}! \q ¡Que todos {{plural_you:sus guerreros|vuestros guerreros}} se adelanten y marchen!

decisions.choice: consecrate war: begin a war with sacred rites
decisions.reason: Armies went to war with sacrifices and prayers to their gods (1 Samuel 7:8-9; Jeremiah 6:4, "consecrate war against her"). The verb is the one used for consecrating a fast in 1:14 and 2:15. Israel was called to a holy fast; the nations are called to a holy war, which will be fought against them.

decisions.choice: proclaim this among the nations: the LORD summons the nations to battle, and to judgment
decisions.reason: The LORD sends heralds to call the nations to arms. The summons is ironic: they think they are coming to fight, but they are coming to the valley where he will judge them (verse 12). The call runs on through verse 11, and is set without quotation marks as the voice of the oracle itself.

decisions.choice: Prepare for holy war (B); Get ready for war (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sense of "consecrate" with "holy war"; Readable says simply "Get ready".

source.text: כֹּ֤תּוּ אִתֵּיכֶם֙ לַֽחֲרָב֔וֹת וּמַזְמְרֹֽתֵיכֶ֖ם לִרְמָחִ֑ים הַֽחַלָּ֔שׁ יֹאמַ֖ר גִּבּ֥וֹר אָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruning knives into spears; the weak, let him say, A warrior [am] I.

en.L: Beat your plowshares into swords \q and your pruning knives into spears; \q let the weak say, \q "I [am] a warrior."
en.B: Hammer your plow blades into swords \q and your knives for pruning into spears. \q Let the weakling say, \q "I am a warrior!"
en.R: Take your blades for plowing and hammer them into swords. \q Turn your knives for trimming vines into spears. \q Even the weak should say, \q "I am a warrior!"

es.L: {{plural_you:Forjen|Forjad}} {{plural_you:sus rejas de arado|vuestras rejas de arado}} en espadas \q y {{plural_you:sus podaderas|vuestras podaderas}} en lanzas; \q diga el débil: \q «Valiente [soy] yo».
es.B: {{plural_you:Martillen|Martillad}} {{plural_you:sus hojas de arado|vuestras hojas de arado}} hasta hacer espadas, \q y {{plural_you:sus cuchillos de podar|vuestros cuchillos de podar}}, lanzas. \q Que el débil diga: \q «¡Soy un guerrero!».
es.R: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} {{plural_you:sus hojas de arar|vuestras hojas de arar}} y {{plural_you:martíllenlas|martilladlas}} hasta convertirlas en espadas. \q {{plural_you:Conviertan|Convertid}} {{plural_you:sus cuchillos para podar las vides|vuestros cuchillos para podar las vides}} en lanzas. \q Que hasta el débil diga: \q «¡Soy un guerrero!».

decisions.choice: Isaiah 2:4 and Micah 4:3 turned around
decisions.reason: Isaiah 2:4 and Micah 4:3 promise that the nations will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning knives, when the LORD judges between them. Here the words are reversed: the nations are told to turn their farm tools into weapons for the war in which the LORD will judge them. Joel uses a different word for "spears" from Isaiah and Micah, a word for a lance. Which passage was spoken first is not known; the reversal is deliberate either way.

decisions.choice: plowshares and pruning knives: iron farm tools
decisions.reason: The first is an iron blade for plowing, the second a knife for trimming vines (Isaiah 2:4; 18:5). Turning them into weapons means every hand and every tool is called to the war.

decisions.choice: let the weak say, "I am a warrior": everyone is called up
decisions.reason: Even the weakest must count himself a fighter. The nations gather every last man, and still they will be judged.

decisions.choice: the wording of Isaiah 2:4, reversed, at each level
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its own wording of Isaiah 2:4 with the direction turned around: "beat ... plowshares ... pruning knives" (L), "hammer ... plow blades ... knives for pruning" (B), "blades for plowing ... knives for trimming vines" (R). Readable says "warrior" as the other levels do, and "the weak" needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: "rejas de arado ... podaderas" (L); "hojas de arado ... cuchillos de podar" (B); "hojas de arar ... cuchillos para podar las vides" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Spanish Isaiah 2:4 at each level, turned around as Joel turns them, so the reader can see the reversal.

source.text: ע֣וּשׁוּ וָבֹ֧אוּ כָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֛ם מִסָּבִ֖יב וְנִקְבָּ֑צוּ שָׁ֕מָּה הַֽנְחַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה גִּבּוֹרֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Hurry and come, all the nations from round about, and gather yourselves. There bring down, Yahweh, your warriors!

en.L: Hurry and come, all you nations round about, and gather yourselves; \q there bring down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} warriors, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.B: Come quickly, all you nations on every side, and gather together! \q Bring down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} warriors there, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.R: Hurry, all you nations around Israel! Come and gather there. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, send down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} warriors to fight them!

es.L: ¡{{plural_you:Dense|Daos}} prisa y {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}, todas las naciones de alrededor, y {{plural_you:reúnanse|reuníos}}! \q ¡Haz descender allí a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} valientes, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}!
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} pronto, todas las naciones de alrededor, y {{plural_you:reúnanse|reuníos}}! \q ¡Haz bajar allí a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} guerreros, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Dense|Daos}} prisa, todas las naciones que rodean a Israel! {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} y {{plural_you:reúnanse|reuníos}} allí. \q {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡envía a {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} guerreros para que peleen contra ellas!

decisions.choice: hurry: a word found only here
decisions.reason: The verb is not found anywhere else, and its meaning is guessed from the context and from related words. "Hurry" or "come to help" fit the line; some ancient translations render it "gather together".

decisions.choice: bring down your warriors, LORD: the prophet breaks in with a prayer
alternatives: a further command to the nations
decisions.reason: In the middle of the summons the prophet turns to the LORD and asks him to send his own warriors down against the gathered nations. These are most likely the LORD's heavenly army, the mighty ones who do his word (Psalm 103:20; Zechariah 14:5). The line is short and abrupt, and the ancient translations read it differently.

decisions.choice: round about: the nations on every side
decisions.reason: The phrase names the nations surrounding Israel, as in verse 12.

decisions.choice: around Israel; to fight them (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says whose surroundings are meant and why the warriors are sent, both implied by the verse.

decisions.choice: tú to the LORD, plural_you to the nations
decisions.reason: The prophet's prayer breaks in with tú and the vocative "SEÑOR" without "oh"; the commands to the nations in verses 9-11 and 13 are plural and take plural_you spans.

source.text: יֵע֨וֹרוּ֙ וְיַעֲל֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֶל־עֵ֖מֶק יְהֽוֹשָׁפָ֑ט כִּ֣י שָׁ֗ם אֵשֵׁ֛ב לִשְׁפֹּ֥ט אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them be roused and come up, the nations, to [the] valley of Jehoshaphat; for there I will sit to judge all the nations from round about.

en.L: Let the nations be roused and come up \q to the valley of Jehoshaphat, \q for there I will sit to judge all the nations round about.
en.B: Let the nations stir themselves and come up \q to the valley of Jehoshaphat, \q for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
en.R: Let the nations get ready and come \q to the valley of Jehoshaphat. \q There I will sit as judge over all the nations around Israel.

es.L: Despiértense y suban las naciones \q al valle de Josafat, \q porque allí me sentaré para juzgar a todas las naciones de alrededor.
es.B: Que las naciones se pongan en marcha y suban \q al valle de Josafat, \q porque allí me sentaré para juzgar a todas las naciones vecinas.
es.R: Que las naciones se preparen y vengan \q al valle de Josafat. \q Allí me sentaré como juez de todas las naciones que rodean a Israel.

decisions.choice: I will sit to judge: take the judge's seat
decisions.reason: A judge or king sat to give judgment (Psalm 9:5, 8; Daniel 7:9-10). The battlefield turns out to be a courtroom, and the LORD presides.

decisions.choice: the valley of Jehoshaphat: the place of judgment, as in verse 2
decisions.reason: "Jehoshaphat" means "the LORD judges", and the next words say "to judge": the name and the action match (see the note at verse 2).

decisions.choice: around Israel (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, Readable says whose surroundings are meant.

source.text: שִׁלְח֣וּ מַגָּ֔ל כִּ֥י בָשַׁ֖ל קָצִ֑יר בֹּ֤אֽוּ רְדוּ֙ כִּֽי־מָ֣לְאָה גַּ֔ת הֵשִׁ֨יקוּ֙ הַיְקָבִ֔ים כִּ֥י רַבָּ֖ה רָעָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Send out [the] sickle, for ripe is [the] harvest; come, tread, for full is [the] winepress; overflow the vats, for great is their evil.

en.L: Send in the sickle, \q for ripe is the harvest; \q come, tread, for full is the winepress; \q the vats overflow, \q for great [is] their evil.
en.B: Swing the sickle, \q for the harvest is ripe. \q Come, tread the grapes, for the winepress is full. \q The vats overflow, \q because their wickedness is great.
en.R: Swing your sickle, \q because the harvest is ready. \q Come and crush the grapes, because the winepress is full. \q The vats are overflowing, \q because these nations are so wicked.

es.L: {{plural_you:Metan|Meted}} la hoz, \q porque madura está la mies; \q {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}, {{plural_you:pisen|pisad}}, porque lleno está el lagar; \q rebosan los lagares, \q porque grande [es] su maldad.
es.B: {{plural_you:Echen|Echad}} mano a la hoz, \q porque la mies está madura. \q {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, {{plural_you:pisen|pisad}} las uvas, porque el lagar está lleno. \q Los lagares rebosan, \q porque su maldad es grande.
es.R: {{plural_you:Usen|Usad}} la hoz, \q porque la cosecha está lista. \q {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} a pisar las uvas, porque el lagar está lleno. \q Los lagares rebosan, \q porque estas naciones son muy malvadas.

decisions.choice: the harvest and the winepress: pictures of judgment
decisions.reason: Cutting the ripe grain and treading grapes in the winepress are pictures of judgment (Isaiah 63:1-6; Jeremiah 25:30). The nations are ripe for it. Revelation 14:14-20 takes up both pictures.

decisions.choice: send in, come, tread: the commands go to the LORD's warriors
decisions.reason: The plural commands most likely continue the prayer of verse 11: the LORD's warriors are told to reap and tread.

decisions.choice: the vats overflow: the words of 2:24
decisions.reason: In 2:24 overflowing vats were the LORD's blessing on his people. Here the same words picture the judgment of the nations, whose wickedness has filled the press.

decisions.choice: these nations (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names whose wickedness is meant.

decisions.choice: "rebosan los lagares"
decisions.reason: The same words as 2:24 at each level, as the Hebrew repeats them.

source.text: הֲמוֹנִ֣ים הֲמוֹנִ֔ים בְּעֵ֖מֶק הֶֽחָר֑וּץ כִּ֤י קָרוֹב֙ י֣וֹם יְהוָ֔ה בְּעֵ֖מֶק הֶחָרֽוּץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For near [is the] day of Yahweh in the valley of decision.

en.L: Multitudes, multitudes \q in the valley of decision! \q For near [is] the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q in the valley of decision.
en.B: Crowds upon crowds \q in the valley of decision! \q Yes, the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is close at hand \q in the valley of decision.
en.R: Huge crowds of people \q are in the valley of decision! \q The day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is close \q in the valley of decision.

es.L: ¡Multitudes, multitudes \q en el valle de la decisión! \q Porque cerca [está] el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} \q en el valle de la decisión.
es.B: ¡Muchedumbres y más muchedumbres \q en el valle de la decisión! \q Sí, el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está a las puertas \q en el valle de la decisión.
es.R: ¡Enormes multitudes de gente \q están en el valle de la decisión! \q El día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está cerca \q en el valle de la decisión.

decisions.choice: the valley of decision: the place where the LORD gives his verdict
decisions.reason: The word means something cut or decided, a verdict (1 Kings 20:40). It is the LORD's decision on the nations, not a decision the people make. The valley is the valley of Jehoshaphat of verses 2 and 12. The same word also names a threshing sledge (Isaiah 28:27; 41:15), which may add the picture of the nations threshed like grain.

decisions.choice: multitudes, multitudes: huge, noisy crowds
decisions.reason: The word means a crowd and also the roar a crowd makes. Repeating it gives the picture of vast armies pressing together.

decisions.choice: the day of the LORD is near: now against the nations
decisions.reason: The words of 1:15 return (see the note there). The day that threatened Judah now falls on the nations gathered for judgment.

decisions.choice: "el valle de la decisión"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets; it looks back to the valley of Jehoshaphat of verses 2 and 12.

source.text: שֶׁ֥מֶשׁ וְיָרֵ֖חַ קָדָ֑רוּ וְכוֹכָבִ֖ים אָסְפ֥וּ נָגְהָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Sun and moon become dark, and stars withdraw their brightness.

en.L: The sun and the moon grow dark, \q and the stars withdraw their shining.
en.B: The sun and moon go dark, \q and the stars lose their brightness.
en.R: The sun and the moon become dark, \q and the stars stop shining.

es.L: El sol y la luna se oscurecen, \q y las estrellas retiran su resplandor.
es.B: El sol y la luna se oscurecen, \q y las estrellas pierden su brillo.
es.R: El sol y la luna se ponen oscuros, \q y las estrellas dejan de brillar.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2:10
decisions.reason: The line repeats 2:10 word for word. The signs that went before the LORD's army against Zion now go before his judgment of the nations.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2:10 at each level
decisions.reason: Each level repeats its wording of 2:10.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2:10
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats 2:10, and the Spanish repeats its own wording of 2:10 at each level.

source.text: וַיהוָ֞ה מִצִּיּ֣וֹן יִשְׁאָ֗ג וּמִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יִתֵּ֣ן קוֹל֔וֹ וְרָעֲשׁ֖וּ שָׁמַ֣יִם וָאָ֑רֶץ וַֽיהוָה֙ מַֽחֲסֶ֣ה לְעַמּ֔וֹ וּמָע֖וֹז לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh from Zion roars, and from Jerusalem gives his voice, and shake heavens and earth; and Yahweh [is] a refuge for his people and a stronghold for [the] children of Israel.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} roars from Zion, and from Jerusalem {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} utters {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, \q and the heavens and the earth shake; \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a refuge for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q and a stronghold for the children of Israel.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} roars from Zion and thunders from Jerusalem, \q and the heavens and the earth tremble. \q But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a refuge for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q a fortress for the people of Israel.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} roars like a lion from Zion. His voice thunders from Jerusalem. \q The sky and the earth shake. \q But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people safe. \q He will be a strong fortress for the people of Israel.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ruge desde Sion, y desde Jerusalén da {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz, \q y tiemblan los cielos y la tierra; \q pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [es] refugio para {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo \q y fortaleza para los hijos de Israel.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ruge desde Sion y truena desde Jerusalén, \q y se estremecen los cielos y la tierra. \q Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es refugio para {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, \q una fortaleza para los israelitas.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ruge como un león desde Sion. Su voz truena desde Jerusalén. \q El cielo y la tierra tiemblan. \q Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mantendrá a salvo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo. \q Él será una fortaleza segura para el pueblo de Israel.

decisions.choice: the LORD roars from Zion: the same words open Amos (Amos 1:2)
decisions.reason: Amos 1:2 begins with the same two lines: "The LORD roars from Zion and from Jerusalem utters his voice." In Amos the roar withers the land; here it shakes heaven and earth against the nations, while the LORD shelters his people. Joel 4:18 also shares words with Amos 9:13.

decisions.choice: roars ... gives his voice: the roar of a lion and the thunder
decisions.reason: The LORD's voice is pictured as a lion's roar (Hosea 11:10; Jeremiah 25:30; Amos 3:8) and as thunder (2:11; Psalm 18:14).

decisions.choice: refuge and stronghold: a place of shelter and a fortress
decisions.reason: The two words picture a shelter from storm and a strong place of safety (Psalm 46:2; Nahum 1:7). The shaking that terrifies the nations leaves God's people safe.

decisions.choice: utters his voice (L); thunders (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "thunders" for "gives his voice", as at 2:11 (Balanced). Readable adds "like a lion" to explain "roars" (m2), and says what "refuge" and "stronghold" mean for the people. Because Amos 1:2 has the same Hebrew, the two verses should share their wording at each level.

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR ruge desde Sion" (shared with Amos 1:2)
decisions.reason: Amos 1:2 opens with the same words, and the Spanish of both verses keeps one wording for them at each level.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" (L); "los israelitas" (B); "el pueblo de Israel" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for these books, with no gender span.

source.text: וִֽידַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם שֹׁכֵ֖ן בְּצִיּ֣וֹן הַר־קָדְשִׁ֑י וְהָיְתָ֤ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ קֹ֔דֶשׁ וְזָרִ֥ים לֹא־יַֽעַבְרוּ־בָ֖הּ עֽוֹד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you will know that I [am] Yahweh your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain; and Jerusalem will be holy, and strangers will not pass through it again.

en.L: And you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q who dwell in Zion, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain; \q and Jerusalem will be holy, \q and strangers will not pass through it again.
en.B: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q living in Zion, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain. \q Jerusalem will be holy, \q and foreigners will never again march through it.
en.R: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. \q I live on Mount Zion, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain. \q Jerusalem will be a holy city, \q and foreign armies will never again pass through it.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, \q que habito en Sion, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} monte santo; \q y Jerusalén será santa, \q y los extraños no pasarán más por ella.
es.B: Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, \q que vivo en Sion, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} monte santo. \q Jerusalén será santa, \q y nunca más pasarán por ella los extranjeros.
es.R: Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}. \q Vivo en el monte Sion, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} monte santo. \q Jerusalén será una ciudad santa, \q y los ejércitos extranjeros nunca más pasarán por ella.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD your God: as in 2:27
decisions.reason: The words of 2:27 return. Then the LORD's presence was the sign of his blessing on the land; here it is the sign of his victory over the nations.

decisions.choice: dwelling in Zion: living among his people
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the LORD dwelling among his people in the tabernacle and temple (Exodus 25:8; 1 Kings 8:12-13). The book ends with the same word (verse 21).

decisions.choice: strangers will not pass through it: foreign invaders will never again overrun it
decisions.reason: "Strangers" here are foreigners who came as conquerors (Obadiah 11; Isaiah 52:1). To "pass through" a city is to march through it as an enemy.

decisions.choice: foreigners (B); foreign armies (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "foreigners" for "strangers" and "march through" for "pass through". Readable says "foreign armies", the sense here (m3).

source.text: וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יִטְּפ֧וּ הֶהָרִ֣ים עָסִ֗יס וְהַגְּבָעוֹת֙ תֵּלַ֣כְנָה חָלָ֔ב וְכָל־אֲפִיקֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יֵ֣לְכוּ מָ֑יִם וּמַעְיָ֗ן מִבֵּ֤ית יְהוָה֙ יֵצֵ֔א וְהִשְׁקָ֖ה אֶת־נַ֥חַל הַשִּׁטִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be in that day, the mountains will drip sweet wine, and the hills will flow [with] milk, and all [the] streambeds of Judah will flow [with] water; and a spring from [the] house of Yahweh will go out and water the valley of the Acacias.

en.L: And it will be in that day [that] the mountains will drip sweet wine, and the hills will flow with milk, \q and all the streambeds of Judah will flow with water; \q and a spring will go out from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and water the valley of Shittim.
en.B: On that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, and milk will flow from the hills; \q all the streambeds of Judah will run with water. \q A spring will flow out from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and water the valley of Shittim.
en.R: At that time sweet wine will drip from the mountains, and milk will flow from the hills. \q Water will fill all the dry streambeds of Judah. \q A spring will flow out from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and water the valley of Shittim.

es.L: Y sucederá en aquel día [que] los montes destilarán vino dulce, y las colinas fluirán leche, \q y todos los arroyos de Judá correrán con agua; \q y saldrá un manantial de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} \q y regará el valle de Sitim.
es.B: Aquel día los montes destilarán vino dulce, y de las colinas fluirá leche; \q por todos los arroyos de Judá correrá el agua. \q Saldrá un manantial de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} \q y regará el valle de Sitim.
es.R: En ese tiempo de los montes goteará vino dulce, y de las colinas fluirá leche. \q El agua llenará todos los arroyos secos de Judá. \q Saldrá un manantial del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} \q y regará el valle de Sitim.

decisions.choice: the mountains will drip sweet wine: the words of Amos 9:13
decisions.reason: Amos 9:13 ends with the same picture: "the mountains will drip sweet wine". The sweet wine that was cut off in 1:5 flows freely. Milk and wine are signs of a land made rich again, like the land "flowing with milk and honey" (Exodus 3:8).

decisions.choice: a spring from the house of the LORD
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 47:1-12 sees a river flowing from the temple that brings life wherever it goes, and Zechariah 14:8 sees living water flowing out from Jerusalem. Revelation 22:1-2 takes up the picture of the river of life.

decisions.choice: the valley of Shittim: the valley of the acacias, its place uncertain
alternatives: the Shittim of Numbers 25:1, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Shittim means acacia trees, which grow in dry ground. The valley may be a dry valley running from Jerusalem towards the Dead Sea, such as the Kidron, or the name may stand for any dry, barren valley, now watered. Shittim was also the name of Israel's last camp east of the Jordan (Numbers 25:1; Joshua 2:1), but that is across the river.

decisions.choice: streambeds: watercourses that are dry for much of the year
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in 1:20 for the channels of water that had dried up. Now they all run with water.

decisions.choice: in that day (L); On that day (B); At that time (R); Shittim (all levels)
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the wording set in Isaiah. Every level keeps the name Shittim, with a footnote on its meaning and place (m3). Readable says "temple" for "the house of the LORD" and "dry streambeds" for the watercourses (m4).

decisions.choice: "el valle de Sitim"
decisions.reason: The name as Joshua 2:1 in Spanish; the meaning footnote explains it as the valley of the acacias.

decisions.choice: "los montes destilarán vino dulce" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Amos 9:13 has the same words, and the Spanish of both keeps one wording.

source.text: מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לִשְׁמָמָ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וֶאֱד֕וֹם לְמִדְבַּ֥ר שְׁמָמָ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֑ה מֵֽחֲמַס֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׁפְכ֥וּ דָם־נָקִ֖יא בְּאַרְצָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Egypt to a desolation will become, and Edom to a wilderness of desolation will become, because of [the] violence [to the] children of Judah, whose innocent blood they shed in their land.

en.L: Egypt will become a desolation, \q and Edom \q a desolate wilderness, \q because of the violence [done to] the children of Judah, \q whose innocent blood they shed in their land.
en.B: Egypt will be laid waste, \q and Edom \q will become a desolate wilderness, \q because of the violence done to the people of Judah, \q whose innocent blood they shed in their land.
en.R: Egypt will become an empty wasteland. \q Edom will become a dry desert. \q This is because of the violence they did to the people of Judah. \q They killed innocent people in Judah's land.

es.L: Egipto se convertirá en desolación, \q y Edom \q en desierto desolado, \q por la violencia [hecha a] los hijos de Judá, \q cuya sangre inocente derramaron en su tierra.
es.B: Egipto quedará devastado, \q y Edom \q se convertirá en un desierto desolado, \q por la violencia que hicieron a la gente de Judá, \q cuya sangre inocente derramaron en su tierra.
es.R: Egipto se convertirá en un desierto vacío. \q Edom se convertirá en un desierto seco. \q Esto será por la violencia que cometieron contra la gente de Judá. \q Mataron a gente inocente en la tierra de Judá.

decisions.choice: Egypt and Edom: old enemies of Judah
decisions.reason: Egypt had invaded Judah and taken its treasures (1 Kings 14:25-26) and killed King Josiah (2 Kings 23:29). Edom, Judah's "brother", is accused of violence against Judah when Jerusalem fell (Obadiah 10-14; Psalm 137:7). The word for "violence" in Obadiah 10 is the one used here.

decisions.choice: the violence of the people of Judah: violence done to them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the violence of the children of Judah", meaning violence that Judah suffered, as "the violence of your brother Jacob" in Obadiah 10.

decisions.choice: in their land: in Judah's land
alternatives: in the lands of Egypt and Edom
decisions.reason: "Their land" most likely means Judah's own land, where Egyptians and Edomites killed its people. It could mean the lands of Egypt and Edom, where people of Judah had fled.

decisions.choice: in Judah's land (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the land (m3).

source.text: וִיהוּדָ֖ה לְעוֹלָ֣ם תֵּשֵׁ֑ב וִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לְד֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Judah forever will remain, and Jerusalem to generation and generation.

en.L: But Judah will be inhabited forever, \q and Jerusalem for generation after generation.
en.B: But Judah will be inhabited forever, \q and Jerusalem for all generations.
en.R: But people will live in Judah forever, \q and in Jerusalem for all generations to come.

es.L: Pero Judá será habitada para siempre, \q y Jerusalén de generación en generación.
es.B: Pero Judá será habitada para siempre, \q y Jerusalén por todas las generaciones.
es.R: Pero la gente vivirá en Judá para siempre, \q y en Jerusalén por todas las generaciones venideras.

decisions.choice: Judah will be inhabited forever: it will remain, full of people
decisions.reason: The verb means to sit or dwell; said of a land or city it means to be inhabited, or to remain in place (Isaiah 13:20; Jeremiah 17:25). Judah stands against Egypt and Edom, left empty in verse 19.

decisions.choice: But (all levels)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and" introduces a contrast with verse 19, which every level marks with "But".

source.text: וְנִקֵּ֖יתִי דָּמָ֣ם לֹֽא־נִקֵּ֑יתִי וַֽיהוָ֖ה שֹׁכֵ֥ן בְּצִיּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will hold innocent their blood [which] I have not held innocent; and Yahweh dwells in Zion.

en.L: And I will hold innocent their blood [that] I have not held innocent, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dwells in Zion.
en.B: I will avenge their blood, which I had left unavenged. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} dwells in Zion.
en.R: I will punish those who shed their blood, which I have not yet done. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} lives in Zion.

es.L: Y declararé inocente su sangre, [la] que no había declarado inocente, \q y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} habita en Sion.
es.B: Vengaré su sangre, que había dejado sin vengar. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} habita en Sion.
es.R: Castigaré a los que derramaron su sangre, cosa que todavía no he hecho. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive en Sion.

decisions.choice: I will hold innocent their blood: I will vindicate the innocent blood of Judah by bringing the guilty to account
alternatives: "Shall I leave their bloodshed unpunished? I will not."
the Greek translation: "I will avenge their blood"
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat as innocent or to leave unpunished, and it plays on "innocent blood" in verse 19. Read with that verse, "their blood" is the innocent blood of the people of Judah, and the LORD will at last declare it innocent by punishing those who shed it. The line is hard, and it has been taken in other ways: as a question, "Shall I leave their bloodshed unpunished? I will not"; or, following the Greek translation, which has "I will avenge", with a different verb. The sense is much the same in each: the LORD will not let the killing of his people go unanswered.

decisions.choice: the LORD dwells in Zion: the book ends with God's presence
decisions.reason: The last words of the book say that the LORD lives among his people. Ezekiel's book ends in the same way: "the LORD is there" (Ezekiel 48:35).

decisions.choice: avenge (B); punish those who shed their blood (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew verb, "hold innocent". Balanced and Readable say what it means here (m1): the LORD will avenge the blood by punishing those who shed it.
